title: When Memory Updates but Behavior Does Not: Repairing Implicit Stale Dependencies in Personalized Agent Responses
title_zh: 当记忆更新而行为不变：修复个性化智能体响应中的隐式陈旧依赖
abstract_en: Memory-augmented agents can know that a user's stored state is outdated and still plan around the old value. The STALE benchmark calls this the implicit policy adaptation (IPA) gap. We identify one structural contributor: draft-anchored verification checks what a response says, and in an open-ended response the stale dependency is usually unsaid. StateAuditor therefore audits in the opposite direction, from stored state to draft. An LLM proposes candidate old-to-new transitions from timestamped evidence; deterministic code pins each quotation to a single entry, checks that the new evidence really is newer, and lets only these verified transitions trigger repair. What is verified is provenance and chronology - not semantic supersession. On STALE's full protocol (400 scenarios, 50-session histories, one independent response per query), strict single-query VTA scores .736 against .686 for our locked predecessor under the same judge: a +5.0-point paired gain (95% CI [+2.9, +7.2]) coming almost entirely from IPA and premise resistance (PR). The benchmark's own judge, from a third model family, reproduces the gain (.738 vs. .680). On an independent cross-family preference-evolution benchmark (HorizonBench), the full draft-audit-repair pipeline over a gold-derived structured store raises current-preference accuracy (user-clustered p<.01), though a matched control shows most of this external gain is the draft-side audit itself; a harder authored lifecycle set gives no gain, bounding the claim while false invalidation stays controlled. On STALE, by contrast, a matched control (same evidence, adapter, and call budget) scores only .692 (+0.6 over the predecessor, n.s.), attributing the STALE gain to the transition machinery rather than added context or calls. We make no claim about general-purpose agent memory.
abstract_zh: 本文研究 memory-augmented agents 中的一个关键问题：即使智能体知道用户存储状态已过时，仍可能在规划响应时依赖旧状态。STALE benchmark 将其称为 implicit policy adaptation（IPA）gap。作者指出，一个结构性原因是 draft-anchored verification 只检查草稿“说了什么”，而在开放式回答中，陈旧依赖通常并不会被显式说出。为此，论文提出 StateAuditor：从存储状态反向审计草稿。具体而言，LLM 先基于带时间戳的证据提出候选 old-to-new transitions；确定性代码再将每段引用绑定到唯一条目，验证新证据确实更新，仅允许通过验证的 transition 触发修复。该验证关注 provenance 与 chronology，而非语义上的 supersession。实验显示，在 STALE 完整协议上，StateAuditor 的严格 single-query VTA 得分为 .736，相比同一评测器下锁定的前代方法 .686 提升 5.0 个百分点，增益主要来自 IPA 与 premise resistance（PR）。第三方模型家族的 benchmark judge 也复现了该提升。在 HorizonBench 上，完整 draft-audit-repair 流水线提升了 current-preference accuracy，但对照实验表明外部收益主要来自 draft-side audit；在更难的 authored lifecycle set 上未观察到提升。STALE 上的匹配对照仅得 .692，说明主要增益来自 transition machinery，而非额外上下文或调用预算。作者不声称该方法适用于通用智能体记忆。
key_points_zh: 论文聚焦 memory-augmented agents 的 IPA gap：记忆已更新，但个性化响应仍隐式依赖旧用户状态。
提出 StateAuditor，从 stored state 到 draft 进行反向审计，而不是只检查草稿中显式陈述的内容。
方法用 LLM 生成候选 old-to-new transitions，并用确定性代码验证引用来源与时间顺序，只有通过验证的 transition 才触发修复。
在 STALE benchmark 上，严格 single-query VTA 从 .686 提升到 .736，主要改善 IPA 与 premise resistance。
跨数据集结果更有限：HorizonBench 有提升但多来自 draft-side audit， authored lifecycle set 无明显收益，作者明确不泛化到通用 agent memory。

llm_assessment.comment: StateAuditor targets an important stale-memory failure mode, though the contribution is relatively narrow and benchmark-bounded.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: StateAuditor 针对重要的过期记忆失效模式，但贡献相对较窄且受基准范围限制。
